tables.name: Nareth Naming Method
tables.description: Ten editable methods for Nareth rainforest and flooded settlement names. Each d100 face is assigned once. Inca-era Quechua geography inspires place-name mechanics; Ixtal informs the rarer ancient architectural atmosphere; no claim of grammatical reconstruction.

results.name: Rivers & Confluences
results.description: Waterways and settlements named after river branches, water colour, springs or river mouths.

results.name: Forest & Canopy
results.description: Canopy, trees, forest clearings, animals and life under heavy vegetation.

results.name: Wetlands & Floodplains
results.description: Flooded woods, lagoons, backwaters and marshes.

results.name: Villages & Cultivated Clearings
results.description: Everyday settlements named after inhabited plots, homes, planted land and enclosures.

results.name: Trails & River Crossings
results.description: River crossings, routes, landings, bridges and travel refuges.

results.name: Ancient Stone & Terraces
results.description: Older built sites, raised plazas, terraces, stone bridges and other durable works.

results.name: Old Geographic Compounds
results.description: Preserves the older fictional Nareth geographic compound vocabulary.

results.name: Ancestral Settlements
results.description: Inherited personal and lineage names; rare, without implying any pre-defined family history.

results.name: Elemental & Hidden Places
results.description: Rare deliberately fictional old-city sounding names, inspired by Ixtal atmosphere.

results.name: Inherited Proper Names
results.description: Rare complete proper names; some preserve the two-word style of Uru Taal.
